# 法華經玄義輯略

**Byline:** 明 傳燈錄
**Dynasty:** 明
**Date:** 1368–1644
**Juans:** 1

## Contributors
- 傳燈 (A007274)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-*juan* abridgement and outline of Zhìyǐ's *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuányì* ([KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006), T1716), recorded by the late-Ming Tiāntái master Yōu-xī Chuándēng 幽溪傳燈 (1554–1628), the principal architect of the late-Ming Tiāntái revival on Tiāntáishān. The text is recorded in the front matter as composed at the *Yōu-xī sēng* 幽溪 retreat ("the *śramaṇa* of Yōu-xī of Tiāntáishān, Chuándēng, recorded": 天台山幽溪沙門　傳燈　錄).

**Abstract**

Chuándēng's *Jílüè* belongs together with Zhìxù's *Jiéyào* ([KR6d0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0010)) as the two principal late-Ming abridgements of Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì*, but Chuándēng's work differs significantly in editorial method: rather than excerpting Zhìyǐ's text verbatim, Chuándēng paraphrases and synthesises, producing what is in effect a self-standing summary in his own voice rather than a condensed copy of the original. The text is consequently more accessible as an introduction but less useful as a study aid alongside the full *Xuányì*.

Yōuxī Chuándēng was the central figure in the late-Ming revival of Tiāntái doctrinal study at Tiāntáishān itself. Born to a Yè 葉 family in Pínghǎi 平海 in modern Zhèjiāng, he took monastic vows at the *Yīnjīngsì* 蔭靜寺; received the dharma from [百際草大師](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BE%E9%9A%9B%E8%8D%89%E5%A4%A7%E5%B8%AB) Bǎijì Cǎo Tàishī of Tiāntái; restored the **Yōuxī Gāomíngsì** 幽溪高明寺 (whence his sobriquet *Yōuxī*) on Tiāntáishān; and produced a substantial corpus of Tiāntái commentaries — the *Wéimó wúwǒ shū* 維摩無我疏 (16 *juan*), the *Lèngyán xuányì* 楞嚴玄義 (4 *juan*), the *Xìngshànè lùn* 性善惡論 (6 *juan*), the *Tiāntái sìjiào yí jízhù* 天台四教儀集註 (10 *juan*), the *Jìngtǔ shēngwúshēng lùn* 淨土生無生論 (1 *juan*), and the present *Xuányì jílüè*. He was the principal Tiāntái dialogue-partner with the late-Ming Pure Land master Yúnqī Zhūhóng 雲棲祩宏 (1535–1615) and the chief late-Ming defender of the *xìngjùè* 性具惡 ("buddha-nature inherently includes evil") doctrine of Sòng Tiāntái scholasticism.

The dating of the *Jílüè* is uncertain — no internal date is given — but it most likely belongs to Chuándēng's mature productive period at Yōuxī Gāomíngsì in the early seventeenth century, alongside his other major Tiāntái compendia.
